summary: A is the less risky patch, but neither is contract-compliant or ready to merge as written.
reasons: A limits generic request replay changes to seekable readers; B eagerly buffers every non-replayable RawClient body, changing streaming and memory behavior across the SDK.
B's makeBodyReplayable silently ignores io.ReadAll errors after potentially consuming part of the source, which can produce truncated requests instead of reliably propagating reader failures.
A directly tests Upload retry with multipart filename and content on both attempts. B does not test Upload retry and records only the final body in its lower-level retry tests.
A at least makes established WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions values usable with Upload. B introduces duplicate WithAddFileQuery and WithAddFileRequestOptions machinery.
risks_a: Upload has the wrong signature: it accepts ...UploadFileOption instead of the required ...FilesOption.
Upload duplicates Add's request, decoding, and error logic through Raw.Do instead of routing through Add.

It adds prohibited association/form-field APIs and changes public option return types, violating scope and FilesOption stability requirements editionsally throughout docs and changelog changes? Actually avoid typo. It also lacks a source-reader failure test.
risks_b: Upload has the wrong ...AddFileOption signature, adds prohibited association fields, and bypasses Add.
Global buffering in RawClient removes streaming behavior, can consume unbounded memory, and may leak or alter closure semantics of caller-supplied readers.

Reader errors during replay preparation are discarded, creating a concrete truncation/error-semantics defect and conflicting with the source-reader failure requirement. It also lacks an Upload retry and source-reader error test.
